subject: siamese cat
title: What If a Cat Co-Wrote a Physics Paper? In 1975 One Did

scenes.text: What if a cat got published in a top physics journal? In 1975, one did.
A Michigan State physicist finishes a paper on helium at ultra-low temperatures. He has written we all the way through.
A colleague points out the problem: he's the only author. And the whole thing is already typed.
So he adds a co-author: F. D. C. Willard. That's Felis Domesticus Chester, his Siamese cat. Willard was the cat's father.
The journal publishes it. The secret slips out when a visitor asks to meet Willard.
Friends get copies signed with a paw print. And in 1980, the cat publishes again, in French, as sole author.

description:
What if a cat co-wrote a physics paper? In 1975 Jack Hetherington of Michigan State University had typed a whole paper on helium-3 using the word we, although he was its only author. Rather than retype it, he added a co-author: F. D. C. Willard, for Felis Domesticus Chester, his Siamese cat (Willard was the cat's father).
Physical Review Letters published it. He later sent friends copies signed with a paw print, and in 1980 Willard appeared as the sole author of an article in the French magazine La Recherche.
